relationships.subject: TLR4-stimulated cytokine/chemokine release
relationships.evidence_quote: we found that greater ex vivo TLR4-stimulated cytokine/chemokine release was associated with the presence of COPCs ( P < 0.01), extent of widespread pain ( P < 0.05), but not experimental pain sensitivity ( P > 0.05)

relationships.subject: TLR4-stimulated cytokine/chemokine release
relationships.evidence_quote: The number of painful regions indicated on the body map (severity ≥ 4) was positively and significantly associated with the TLR4 global composite score (p < .05)

relationships.subject: TAK-242
relationships.evidence_quote: administration of TAK-242, a TLR4 antagonist[25], in cystitis-induced URO-OVA mice reduced pain sensitization

key_findings: Higher ex vivo TLR4-stimulated whole-blood cytokine release was associated with COPCs and widespread pain in female IC/BPS patients.
A second anti-inflammatory/chemotactic component was associated with lower pressure pain sensitivity.
